nodes.description: Public address state variable holding the contract owner, set from msg.sender in the constructor and used as beneficiary of ownerWithdraw and selfdestruct.
Mapping address => uint tracking pending withdrawal balances; written by userRegister reward logic and zeroed before transfer in userWithdraw.
Unsigned integer tracking the current game round; incremented in userRegister and used to index the participants mapping.
Mapping uint => address[3] storing the three participants (owner/registrant/winner) of each round.
Access-control modifier requiring msg.sender == owner before executing the guarded function body.
Owner-only external function transferring an arbitrary amount to the owner address.
Owner-only external function that selfdestructs the contract and sends remaining balance to owner.
Public view function returning the current round value.
Public view function returning the address[3] participant list for a given round index.
Public view function returning the pending withdrawal balance of a given address.
Public function that reads withdrawals[msg.sender], zeroes it, and transfers the amount to the caller.
Payable public function taking a 105 finney entry fee, storing the caller as participant, computing a pseudo-random winner, crediting a 100 finney reward and advancing the round.
Constructor setting owner = msg.sender, round = 1 and seeding participants[1][0] with the owner.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership checks, participant registration and as the recipient of withdrawal transfers.
External value transfer from the contract to the owner address, sending an amount chosen by the owner.
Destructive selfdestruct call that permanently removes the contract code and forwards the balance to owner.
External value transfer of the caller's recorded withdrawal balance to the untrusted msg.sender.
Unchecked addition crediting a 100 finney reward to the winner's pending withdrawal balance.
Unchecked increment of the round counter state variable at the end of userRegister.
Winner selection driven by uint(blockhash(block.number - 1)) combined with participant addresses, a miner-influenceable source of pseudorandomness.
Caller-supplied amount parameter of ownerWithdraw used as the transfer value.
Caller-supplied round index parameter of publicGetParticipants used to select the participants array.
Caller-supplied address parameter of publicGetBalance used as lookup key into the withdrawals mapping.
Local variable caching withdrawals[msg.sender] before it is zeroed and transferred.
Local constant of 100 finney credited to the winner's withdrawal balance.
Local pseudo-random value derived from blockhash and participant addresses, used to pick the winner.

edges.reason: Caller-controlled msg.sender is compared against the owner state variable inside the whenOwner modifier.
whenOwner modifier gates execution of the ownerWithdraw function body.
whenOwner modifier gates execution of the ownerDestroy function body.
The amount parameter flows directly into the owner.transfer call value.
The owner state variable is the recipient of the owner.transfer value transfer.
The owner state variable is the beneficiary of the selfdestruct call.
Constructor assigns the owner state variable directly from the untrusted msg.sender.
owner state variable is initialized from msg.sender during contract construction.
Constructor initializes the round state variable to 1.
msg.sender keys the withdrawals lookup and is the recipient of the transfer in userWithdraw.
withdrawals[msg.sender] is read for the balance check and amount assignment.
The recorded withdrawal balance is transferred out to the untrusted caller.
Local amount variable supplies the value passed to msg.sender.transfer.
External value transfer is made to the untrusted msg.sender address.
The external transfer call is executed inside the userWithdraw function after state update.
The withdrawals mapping is incremented by the reward amount for the winner.
Local reward constant is added into the withdrawals mapping without overflow checks.
Reward crediting addition is executed within the userRegister function branch.
The round++ operation writes the incremented value back into the round state variable.
The round counter increment is executed within userRegister.
The round state variable indexes the participants mapping inside userRegister.
userRegister writes the caller address into the participants mapping for the current round.
The local random value is computed from blockhash and participant addresses in userRegister.
Weak blockhash-derived randomness determines which branch pays the reward in userRegister.
The random local variable is defined and computed within userRegister.
The reward local variable is defined within userRegister.
msg.sender supplies the entry fee and is stored as a round participant in userRegister.
Local amount variable is assigned from the caller's withdrawals balance in userWithdraw.
The amount parameter belongs to and is consumed by ownerWithdraw.
The index parameter belongs to and is consumed by publicGetParticipants.
The index parameter selects the round entry read from the participants mapping.
publicGetParticipants returns the participants array selected by the index.
The player parameter indexes the withdrawals mapping.
publicGetBalance reads the withdrawals mapping for the queried player.
publicGetRound returns the current round state variable.
The player parameter belongs to and is consumed by publicGetBalance.

normalization_plan.reason: The amount parameter has no independent state effect and only feeds the owner.transfer value transfer.
The index parameter is only used to select the participants array returned by publicGetParticipants.
The player parameter is only used as the lookup key for the withdrawals read in publicGetBalance.
The local amount variable exists only to carry the withdrawal balance into msg.sender.transfer.
The local reward constant is only used to increment the withdrawals mapping.
The local random variable is only used for the blockhash-based winner selection operation.
